newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian politicians praise swimmer Susie Maroney.
newsitem.headline: Australian politicians praise swimmer Susie Maroney.

text.p: Australian politicians were quick off the blocks on Tuesday in praising record-setting swimmer Susie Maroney after she became the first person to swim from Cuba to Florida.

"On behalf of all Australians I wish to congratulate you on your truly outstanding achievement in being the first person to swim the Straits of Florida," Australian Prime Minister John Howard said in a statement.

Maroney, 22, walked ashore in Key West, Florida, on Monday after 24-and-a-half hours in the water swimming the 108 miles (174 km) from Havana. She had battled threatening conditions and choppy seas which damaged her protective shark cage.

Howard, whose conservative government was negotiating the skark-infested waters of Australia's economy ahead of releasing its second budget later on Tuesday, said all Australians had been behind Maroney.
"Your courageous and successful fight against the elements and never-say-die attitude are an inspiration to us all and serve as a reminder to the world of what Australians can achieve," Howard said.

New South Wales state premier Bob Carr, who is also the local parliamentary member for Maroney's beachside Sydney suburb of Maroubra, said a state reception would be held for the swimmer when she returned.
"Susie Maroney is a shining example of the rewards of motivation and hard work," Carr said in a statement.
Federal opposition Labor leader Kim Beazley said "it does your heart good" to watch an achievement such as Maroney's.
"To see her showing Aussie fortitude globally is just terrific," Beazley told reporters.

Beazley's deputy, former Australian foreign minister Gareth Evans, was not beyond using Maroney's exploits to score political points off Howard, who has suffered in recent polls for perceived weak leadership over key issues.

"What John Howard badly needs now is a touch of the Susie Maroneys -- a sense of direction, some stamina, some purpose and a capacity to be a real inspiration to the country," Evans said. Estimates vary on the number of previous attempts to swim between Cuba and the U.S. mainland, a crossing which had been considered one of swimming's last great challenges.
But Connie Pignatiello, a U.S. coordinator of Maroney's swim, said the trip completed on Monday was the 21st attempt.
